behavior_before: The SQLite knowledge index could inventory an explicitly supplied path but had no governed admission contract, metadata/no-content policy enforcement, bounded work queue, or provider-result ingestion boundary.
behavior_after: The existing owner validates the governed theestate worktree before traversal, inventories only admitted policy paths, records scope/boundary state, selects resumable bounded batches, builds content-limited provider packets, and ingests candidate-only results with provenance, idempotency, and conflict protection.
expected_inputs: provider result keyed to assigned asset IDs
new_failure_modes: provider result outside assigned batch rejected
incompatible provider result or self-promotion rejected
changed_failure_modes: full repository inventory is deterministic and bounded by policy rather than arbitrary CLI roots
validation_evidence: 5,826 admitted assets inventoried in 38.06 seconds at committed revision
one three-asset and three two-asset provider packets across diagnostics, Estate core, and troubleshooting scopes
candidate ingestion idempotency and conflict preservation
preliminary_troubleshooting_notes: If a population run times out, inspect the exact worker process and SQLite lock; do not widen scope or kill unrelated Estate services. Re-run the bounded governed scan after the lock is reconciled.
prohibited_recovery_actions: Do not scan C: or arbitrary A: siblings
Do not let providers add paths
Do not send metadata-only/no-content assets to providers
Do not launch unattended AI population
activation_restart_impact: No daemon or scheduler restart; migration 2 is applied when the existing CLI opens the runtime projection. The current local SQLite writer boundary remains.
